newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rioters attack Chinese houses.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rioters attack Chinese houses.

text.p: Indonesian rioters attacked the homes of ethnic Chinese around a town in central Java on Wednesday during a rampage apparently sparked by reports that a popular singer had switched political allegiances, residents said.
"A number of houses belonging to the Chinese have been either damaged or burned," a Chinese man told Reuters by phone from Pekalongan, a coastal town about 300 km (190 miles) east of Jakarta.
Police said the situation was under control, but refused to give further details. Residents said police and troops were patrolling the streets, but there were no reports of casualties.
"We don't dare to go out. Many shops are closed and soldiers are seen in many parts of the town," a resident said by phone.
"It seems that the target is the Chinese even though they have nothing to do with what has happened," another resident said.
It was the first violence in Java since a mob attacked Chinese homes and businesses, Christian churches and Buddhist temples in the town of Tasikmalaya in western Java in January.
Four people died in those riots, set off by an incident of police brutality against a Moslem teacher.
Ethnic disturbances between local Dayaks and immigrant Madurese also rocked West Kalimantan province on Borneo island last month. At least 12 people died, military officials and residents said.
Residents in Pekalongan said the latest violence was apparently triggered by anger over the planned appearance of popular singer Rhoma Irama in the town of about 135,000 people.
Some residents said people had also been angered over a rumour that a soldier had shot a member of the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP).
Residents said Irama had apparently been a supporter of the PPP but now was a parliamentary candidate for the ruling Golkar party.
The PPP, Golkar and the Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) are the only political groups legally permitted to contest general elections due to be held on May 29.
The official Antara news agency said the stage due to have been used by the singer was burned on Monday and 16 people had been questioned by the authorities.
Residents said graffiti denouncing the singer had been scrawled on many shops in Pekalongan.
Sociologists and political analysts have blamed several riots over the past few months on socio-economic tensions and anger over police brutality and local corruption.
